How can I change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
To change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its unique shape and glaze material, you can use several digital techniques ranging from manual perspective tools to generative AI. Because ceramic surfaces have complex curves, lighting reflections, and distinct textures, changing the angle requires tools that respect 3D depth rather than just flattening the image. 
magiceraser.live
 +1
Here are the best methods to achieve this:
1. Use Generative AI View-Synthesis Tools (Best for Realistic Material Preservation)
Modern e-commerce AI platforms specialize in turning a single, flat product photo into an interactive 3D model or generating entirely new camera angles. 
YouTube
·DolphyAI
How it works: You upload your original ceramic photo into an AI product photography tool. Using a chat-based dashboard or custom prompt interface, you specify the desired viewpoint (e.g., "Change the camera angle to a three-quarter view while maintaining product shape, texture, and glaze consistency").
The Benefit: AI tools handle the complex light reflections and dynamic ranges of curved ceramic surfaces better than standard distortion filters, ensuring the glaze looks natural from the new angle. You can explore tutorials like the YouTube AI Product Turnaround Guide to see how these prompts generate seamless new angles. 
magiceraser.live
 +1
2. Photoshop Perspective Warp (Best for Manual Precision)
If you prefer precise control and want to avoid the unpredictability of generative AI, Adobe Photoshop offers a dedicated 3D perspective tool. 
TikTok
·piximperfects
How to do it:
Duplicate your layer (Ctrl/Cmd + J) and navigate to Filter > Convert for Smart Filters.
Go to Edit > Perspective Warp.
Draw a grid plane over the face of the ceramic item, then define adjacent planes to map its physical volume.
Switch the tool from Layout mode to Warp mode at the top menu bar to manipulate the pins and shift the object into a three-quarter angle. 
TikTok
·piximperfects
Limitation: Since ceramics are highly curved, you must carefully align multiple small planes to map the contours without stretching or blowing out the highlight textures. 
magiceraser.live
 +1
3. Canva's Transform Image App (Best for Quick, Basic Adjustments)
For simple, boxier ceramic items (like geometric planters or square tiles), you can use graphic design tools to skew the 3D plane. 
Canva
 +1
How to do it: Inside the Canva Design Platform, open the side menu, go to "Apps," and search for the Transform Image App by Simon Both. Upload your photo with a transparent background, then drag the corner handles to tilt the perspective into a simulated three-quarter angle. 
Canva
 +2
Limitation: This treats the photo like a flat card being tilted in space, meaning you won't actually reveal the hidden "side" or inside of a hollow ceramic vessel.

Comparison Overview
Method	Best For	Shape Preservation	Material & Glaze Realism
Generative AI	Automatic view generation and showing hidden sides	High (if prompted well)	High (re-calculates lighting and glaze texture)
Photoshop Perspective Warp	Experienced editors needing exact geometric control	High (manually controlled)	Medium (stretching may distort reflections)
Canva Transform	Fast mockups of flat or angular ceramic objects	Low (flattens the object)	Low (purely skews existing pixels)
To recommend the best tool for your project, could you tell me:
What type of ceramic product is it (e.g., a round vase, a mug with a handle, a flat plate)?
Does the item have a glossy, reflective glaze or a matte texture?
Do you have Photoshop, or would you prefer a free online tool?
